$comment: AUTHORITY for what a registry of knowledge bases keeps in a SessionStorage, and what the sessions it makes keep there: the key each thing is kept under, the shape of a knowledge base's stored session, the shape of a resource open in one, the shape of a sign-in by a page redirect that is under way, and what a client keeps of its queries and of its stream. A registry in any SDK finds what one in another wrote, over one storage, only if every SDK says these alike. WHO HOLDS IT. TypeScript states it by hand in packages/typescript/sdk/src/session/storage.ts, oauth.ts and open-resource.ts, held by packages/typescript/sdk/src/session/__tests__/stored-table.test.ts and oauth.test.ts. Rust in packages/rust/sdk/src/session/stored.rs and open_resource.rs, held by packages/rust/sdk/tests/tables.rs, and in packages/rust/http-transport/src/oauth.rs, held by packages/rust/http-transport/tests/sign_in.rs. Go in packages/go/sdk/registry/stored.go and openresource.go, held by packages/go/sdk/registry/stored_test.go, and in packages/go/sdk/authorization.go and storage.go, held by packages/go/sdk/stored_test.go. Kotlin in packages/kotlin/sdk/src/main/kotlin/semiont/registry/Stored.kt and Open.kt and semiont/http/Authorization.kt, held by packages/kotlin/sdk/src/test/kotlin/semiont/registry/StoredTest.kt and semiont/http/AuthorizationTest.kt. Swift in packages/swift/sdk/Sources/Semiont/Registry/Stored.swift, OpenResources.swift and RedirectSignIn.swift, held by packages/swift/sdk/Tests/SemiontTests/RegistryTablesTests.swift and IssuerTests.swift; its generator, packages/swift/sdk/Sources/SemiontCodegen/Tables.swift, makes its stored session of `storedSession`. C# reads the table, which its generator (packages/csharp/sdk/generators/Semiont.Generator/ProtocolGenerator.cs) embeds, in packages/csharp/sdk/src/Semiont/Registry/RegistryStorage.cs, where it states the open resource, and states the pending sign-in in packages/csharp/sdk/src/Semiont/Authorization/RedirectSignIn.cs, held by packages/csharp/sdk/tests/Semiont.Tests/RegistryTests.cs. Python: packages/codegen/schemas/generate-stored-python.mjs writes packages/python/sdk/src/semiont/stored.py, and packages/python/sdk/tests/test_registry_http.py holds the pending sign-in of packages/python/sdk/src/semiont/http/oauth.py. Haskell: packages/haskell/sdk/codegen/Main.hs generates its keys and prefixes (packages/haskell/sdk/generated/Semiont/Internal/Generated/Stored.hs) and its stored session, pending sign-in and open resource (Models/StoredSession.hs, PendingAuthorization.hs and OpenResource.hs beside it) from the table. What a client keeps of its queries and of its stream (`wholeKey`, `cacheDocument`, `lastEventIds`) every SDK holds by running protocol/specs/src/session/cache-cases.json against its own persister: what it writes, and what it keeps of what another wrote. READING IT. `keys` are the fixed keys, each named as protocol/specs/src/client/surface.json names its constant. A knowledge base's session is kept under `sessionKeyPrefix` followed by the knowledge base's id, and `storedSession` is what is kept there, as JSON: a flat object schema whose every member is text. `lastEventIdKeyPrefix` and `cacheKeyPrefix` begin the keys of what a session keeps of its stream and its queries for one person, as each one's `docs` says, and each one's `example` is one key worked out from a knowledge base's id, a person's did and, for a query, its name. The queries a client keeps across a restart are those protocol/specs/src/client/refresh.json marks `persisted`, each kept as a `cacheDocument` under `cacheKeyPrefix`, its entries' values what the query's `value` there says its cache holds. An entry's key is a resource's id for a query `per` resource, an annotation's id for one `per` annotation, and `wholeKey` for one per nothing; a query per filters is not kept. A load keeps nothing of a document whose structure is not `cacheDocument`'s (not JSON, not an object, of another version, its `entries` not a list, or an entry not a key, a value and a stamp), and skips an entry whose key or value is not what its query keeps. A load of `lastEventIds` skips a pair that is not a resource's id and a PersistedEventId, and keeps none of a value that is no object. `pendingAuthorization` is what is kept under `pendingAuthorizationKey`, and `openResource` each entry of a list kept under `openResourcesByKbKey`, as JSON; a member either does not require is not written when there is none.

keys.docs: The registered knowledge bases: a JSON list of KnowledgeBase (components/schemas/KnowledgeBase.json).
The id of the active knowledge base. Nothing is kept under it while none is active.
What is open in each knowledge base: a JSON object from a knowledge base's id to the list of its open resources, each an `openResource`.
Where the person was in each knowledge base: a JSON object from a knowledge base's id to the id of the resource last viewed in it.

A sign-in by a page redirect that is under way: what it remembers across the trip to the issuer and back. It is taken when the sign-in completes, so a callback that is replayed finds nothing to complete.

sessionKeyPrefix.docs: A knowledge base's stored session is kept under this followed by the knowledge base's id.

lastEventIdKeyPrefix.docs: Where a knowledge base's stream was, for one person, is kept under this followed by the knowledge base's id, a dot and the person's key: the unpadded base64url SHA-256 of the UTF-8 of the did the gateway answers for the person's token (components/schemas/UserResponse.json), never the did itself. What is kept is `lastEventIds`. It is written in the same call as a write of one of the caches kept beside it, and only while every kept cache has no fetch in flight and owes no save, and the refresher owes no refetch (a window of B19, protocol/contract/CACHE-SEMANTICS.md, that holds an invalidation it has not yet run); so it never leads them. Its own write is never a reason to write a cache. At disposal this is read once, before any kept cache or the refresher is disposed. Nothing is kept for a token whose person the gateway has not named, and forgetting the knowledge base's stored sign-in, however it is forgotten, deletes it.

cacheKeyPrefix.docs: What a client keeps of a query, for one person, is kept under this followed by the knowledge base's id, a dot, the person's key as `lastEventIdKeyPrefix` makes it, a dot and the query's name: one `cacheDocument` for each query protocol/specs/src/client/refresh.json marks `persisted`. Nothing is kept for a token whose person the gateway has not named, and forgetting the knowledge base's stored sign-in, however it is forgotten, deletes the key of every kept query.

wholeKey.docs: The key a kept query that is per nothing (a `queries` row of protocol/specs/src/client/refresh.json with no `per`) keeps its one entry under.

storedSession.title: StoredSession
storedSession.description: What is kept of a sign-in: the tokens an issuer issued, the client they were issued to, and the issuer's endpoints a renewal and a sign-out need, learned once at sign-in so no session asks again. TOKENS, never a password. A stored value that lacks a member it requires is no session.

access.description: The access token: short-lived, sent as a Bearer token.

refresh.description: The refresh token: what renews the access token at the issuer without another sign-in.

clientId.description: The client the tokens were issued to, which a renewal and a revocation name.

tokenEndpoint.description: The issuer's token endpoint, where the refresh grant is made.

revocationEndpoint.description: The issuer's revocation endpoint (RFC 7009), where a sign-out tells it to forget the refresh token. Absent when the issuer has none.

personKey.description: Who the gateway said the sign-in's person is, as the key their caches and stream position are kept under (`lastEventIdKeyPrefix`), never the did itself. Written once the gateway names the person, on the sign-in whose token it was asked about; a renewal keeps it, a new sign-in starts without it, and forgetting the sign-in, however it is forgotten, reads it first to delete what is kept under it. Absent for a sign-in whose gateway has not yet named its person.

pendingAuthorization.title: PendingAuthorization
pendingAuthorization.description: What a sign-in by a page redirect remembers across the trip to the issuer and back: the verifier and the state the issuer's response must match, where the person was connecting, what they believed they were connecting to, and the issuer's endpoints, so its completion asks nothing twice.

state.description: What the issuer's response must carry back to belong to this sign-in: random, as base64url.

verifier.description: The PKCE code verifier (RFC 7636) the authorization code is exchanged with: random, as base64url.

redirectUri.description: Where the issuer sends the person back to, named again when the code is exchanged.

issuer.description: The issuer the knowledge base trusts, and the endpoints of it a client uses.

authorization.description: The issuer's authorization endpoint, where the person is sent.

token.description: The issuer's token endpoint, where the code is exchanged.

device.description: The issuer's device authorization endpoint (RFC 8628). Absent when the issuer has none.

revocation.description: The issuer's revocation endpoint (RFC 7009). Absent when the issuer has none.

kbId.description: The registered knowledge base being signed in to again. Absent when it is none.

expectedDid.description: The did of what the person believed they clicked, checked against the answer and never assumed. Absent when they named nothing.

expectedName.description: The name of what the person believed they clicked. Absent when they named nothing.

openResource.title: OpenResource
openResource.description: A resource open in a knowledge base: which resource, the name it is shown by, when it was opened and its place among the others open there. A registry shows them by their places, and two in one place by when each was opened, first first.

name.description: The name the resource is shown by.

openedAt.description: When the resource was opened, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Opening it again while it is open changes neither this nor its place.

order.description: The resource's place among those open in the knowledge base. One opened is given the place after the last taken, so a place freed by closing one is not given twice; a move gives each its place in the new order, counted from 0.

mediaType.description: The resource's media type, which its icon is chosen by. Absent when it is not known.

storageUri.description: Where the resource is in the knowledge base's working tree, as a URI (file://docs/overview.md). Absent when it is not known.

cacheDocument.title: CacheDocument
cacheDocument.description: What a client keeps of one query: each key it was asked of, the value its answer gave, and when that value was received.

version.description: The form of the document. A document of another version is read as none.

entries.description: The query's kept keys. A document larger than `maxStoredBytesCount` (protocol/specs/src/client/timing.json) loses the entries received longest ago until it fits.

prefixItems.description: The key: a resource's id for a query per resource, an annotation's id for one per annotation, `wholeKey` for one per nothing.
The value: what the query's `value` in protocol/specs/src/client/refresh.json says its cache holds.
When the value was received, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. A value received again unchanged (its JSON text the text it was kept with) keeps the time it was first received.

lastEventIds.title: LastEventIds
lastEventIds.description: Where a knowledge base's stream was: for each scope, a resource's id, the id of the last recorded event delivered on it.
